findings: Solved 2026-10-29 on the owner's request (Practice, Book exercises, as the Computer Science exercises): the Chapter 7 exercise (PDF 170-173, printed 167-170) in English and Roman Urdu. 12 MCQs as keyed checkpoints, 7 short, 5 constructed response and 7 comprehensive questions and 10 numerical problems as self-checks with model answers; comparisons (7.2, 7.4 short; 7.3 CRQ) as two-column answer tables. Drafts for the academic review.
MCQ key worked out from the chapter (the book prints none): 1a 2a 3c 4a 5c 6a 7b 8c 9b 10d 11c 12b.
MCQ 7.9: options (b) mechanical, (c) pressure and (d) longitudinal all describe sound in air; keyed (b) per the chapter's classification (7.1), with a Book correction box.

MCQ 7.10: the option exponents are printed very small in a low-resolution scan; read as 10³-10⁵, 10⁵-10⁷, 10⁷-10⁹, 10⁹-10¹¹ Hz. The microwave frequency range is not given in the chapter (7.7 gives only mm-cm wavelengths); answer (d) derived from f = c/λ (beyond the chapter).

All ten printed numerical answers were checked and agree (2 Hz; 600 m s⁻¹; 314 Hz; 76.2 Hz; 3.6 × 10⁶ J; 4 W m⁻⁴, 2.24 m; 1.33 and 0.25 W m⁻²; 4 × 10⁻⁷ W m⁻²; 170/340/510 and 85/255/425 Hz; 1079.4 and 931.5 Hz). No book corrections in the numericals.

Beyond the chapter (labelled in the answers): persistence of hearing (~1/10 s) in CRQ 7.5; the vibrator-and-pulley laboratory set-up in Comprehensive 7.2; laser/two-slit examples of coherent sources (short 7.3).
